title: Standardize SDK release attestations and publish CI for streaming/retry examples
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Goal: Create a repeatable, auditable CI+publish pipeline that builds, attests, signs, and publishes SDK artifacts for Python, TypeScript, and Go, and simultaneously publish canonical streaming and retry usage examples across the three SDKs. Deliverables: 1) CI workflows (GitHub Actions) that produce reproducible artifacts for PyPI/npm/go modules, produce SLSA-style provenance metadata, and cosign signatures for published artifacts; 2) canonical example repos demonstrating streaming ergonomics and retry/backoff best practices for text streaming and long-lived connections; 3) a staging dry-run that pushes artifacts to a private test registry (TestPyPI/NPM/registery) and verifies installation and runtime behavior; 4) docs and runbook for signing key rotation and emergency unpublish. Acceptance criteria: - All three languages have CI workflows that create deterministic artifacts and attach provenance JSON to the GitHub release. - Artifacts are signed (cosign) and verification documented. - Streaming examples show consistent retry semantics and backpressure handling across SDKs. - End-to-end smoke tests validate install + streaming examples in a fresh container. Success metrics: publishing latency < 10m for non-binary builds, reproducible checksum across two independent runners, and zero regressions in streaming sample behaviors between languages. Trade-offs and constraints: - Python manylinux wheels with native extensions complicate bit-for-bit reproducibility; we will prioritize reproducible metadata and deterministic wheel build flags and fall back to source-distribution verification where binary determinism is infeasible. - Centralized signing keys vs per-language maintainers: initial plan uses a central signing service (CI-owned KMS) to keep rollout simple; long-term we will design per-repo delegation via sigstore OIDC flows. - Avoid coupling release CI to runtime infra (no production credentials in publish pipeline); use ephemeral artifacts in staging and gated approvals for real publish. Rollout plan: - Phase 1: Implement CI for build+provenance+signature for python (dry-run to TestPyPI) and a canonical streaming example in python. - Phase 2: Implement same for TypeScript and Go, run cross-language smoke tests. - Phase 3: Wire automated publish with manual approval step and update SDK docs + release checklist. Contact points: release-eng (Ben R.), SDK maintainers (Deepa I., Carlos M.), security (Ethan P.).
